title: Homogeneous attractive Bose-Einstein condensates with repulsive three-body interactions: the two-dimensional case
abstract: We consider a homogeneous Bose gas composed of $N$ identical bosons occupying an infinite two-dimensional space. This gas exhibits both an attractive two-body interaction and a repulsive three-body interaction. Via the intermediate Hartree theory, we rigorously derive the homogeneous cubic-quintic nonlinear Schroedinger functional as the mean-field limit of the model. Our investigation focuses on the system's behavior in relation to the two-body interaction.
summary: This paper investigates a Bose gas in 2D with both attractive two-body and repulsive three-body interactions. It uses the Hartree theory to derive the effective cubic-quintic nonlinear Schrödinger equation governing the mean-field limit. The core contribution is establishing the mathematical conditions under which the quantum ground state energy converges to known limiting forms, such as the Thomas-Fermi or pure NLS solutions.
main_problem: To rigorously derive the homogeneous cubic-quintic nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) functional as the mean-field limit of a quantum many-body Hamiltonian describing a Bose gas.
main_result: The paper establishes conditions for the existence of NLS ground states and derives the asymptotic limits of the quantum ground state energy, showing convergence to cubic-quintic, cubic, or Thomas-Fermi approximations.
method: The analysis employs the intermediate Hartree theory and rigorous asymptotic analysis by taking the large-$N$ limit under various scaling assumptions for the interaction parameters.
model_or_system: The system is a homogeneous Bose gas of $N$ identical bosons in two dimensions ($\mathbb{R}^2$) characterized by both an attractive two-body interaction and a repulsive three-body interaction.
key_observables: Ground state energy per particle ($E_{QM}$), the NLS ground state energy ($E_{	ext{NLS}}$), and the Thomas-Fermi (TF) energy functional.
important_parameters: Interaction strengths ($a$ for two-body, $b$ for three-body), the number of particles ($N$), and critical interaction values ($a^*$).
main_assumptions: The derivation of the NLS functional requires the large-$N$ limit, and the analysis relies on specific scaling regimes for the interaction parameters.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first deriving the mean-field NLS functional from the full Hamiltonian using the Hartree ansatz, followed by establishing theorems regarding the existence of ground states and analyzing the convergence of the quantum energy to various mean-field limits (Cubic-quintic, Cubic, TF).
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed mathematical framework for understanding the mean-field behavior of interacting quantum gases, particularly when multiple interaction terms (two-body and three-body) are present, which is crucial for modeling real-world ultracold atomic systems.
